result.title: Saying No by Asking Yes: Affirmative Decomposition and Evidence Reflection for Frozen CLIP
result.summary: Frozen vision-language models often match concepts mentioned in a caption without respecting their negation: a query "a kitchen with no toaster" favors an image containing a toaster. Yet these models are substantially stronger at matching affirmative descriptions. We exploit this asymmetry with Negation-Aware Evidence Scoring (NAES), which reformulates negated descriptions into affirmative queries and combines their evidence by caption structure. A lightweight text decomposer, NegSplit, identifies this structure by extracting negated spans and the remaining affirmative context. For captions with an affirmative remainder, NAES matches that content and applies a presence-based correction for the denial. When no affirmative content remains, it queries the denied object's presence and reflects the evidence around a reference to score the negated description. With LAION-2B CLIP, NAES achieves 82.4% accuracy on COCO-MCQ and 93.0% on VOC2007-MCQ, surpassing KTN by 2.9 and 0.9 percentage points; with OpenAI CLIP, it exceeds PeakPatch accuracy by 4.4 and 26.0 points, respectively. NAES also improves negated-description retrieval on COCO and MSR-VTT, with gains extending to SigLIP, SigLIP 2, and larger CLIP encoders. The strongest multiple-choice results use competing descriptions to center and align evidence; retrieval improvements persist without this conditioning. These findings show that explicitly separating affirmative matching from denied-object evidence can substantially improve negation-aware ranking.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对冻结 CLIP 难以处理否定描述的问题，提出 NAES：先用 NegSplit 将描述拆为否定片段与剩余肯定语境，再把否定查询改写为肯定查询，并结合存在性校正与证据反射来改进图文匹配和检索。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「肯定化分解＋证据反射」可为例外于核心 LVR 的视觉证据筛选与答案验证提供方法线索，可供核查；但论文不涉及 latent 状态生成或推理轨迹，与主线的联系仍是间接的。
